region.text: Gorkha (Gorkhakot), the hill principality of Dravya Shah, with 'parts west of Trishuli from present day Dhading' (the Prithvi Narayan Shah page's description of Gorkha's historical extent)

ledger.note: 1559: Dravya Shah founds the Gorkha Kingdom at Gorkha. 'The Gorkha kingdom was established in 1559 CE by Prince Dravya Shah', son of King Yasho Brahma Shah of Lamjung, who 'conquered Gorkhakot from King Mansingh Khadka Magar'. The page gives the place and the year, not an extent (infobox date ranges 1559-1570 are unlabelled).

region.text: the hill fort of Nuwakot north-west of the Nepal Valley, captured 26 September 1744

ledger.note: 26 September 1744: the Gorkhalis take Nuwakot. 'managed to capture the hill fort on September 26, 1744' (Unification of Nepal); the Prithvi Narayan Shah page has 'The Nuwakot army was routed in 1744 CE'. The Unification table adds 'returned to Kathmandu in 1745', which the page's later campaigns and the kathmandu dossier do not follow.

ledger.counterpart: Dolakha and the hill principalities east of the Nepal Valley
ledger.note: 1754: Dolakha and Sindhupalchowk annexed. Unification table, 1754 (1811 BS): 'Dolakha, Sindhupalchowk, Dahachowk and Naldum annexed.' The Prithvi Narayan Shah table has 'Capture of Dolakha and Kirtipur borders' in 1754. The page does not say whose land it was; the circles are my reading of the district names.

region.text: the Nepal Valley of Kathmandu, Lalitpur and Bhaktapur (Cliopatria's Kathmandu shape of 1757)

ledger.note: 1757: the Gorkhalis open the assault on the Nepal Valley. 'In 1757, The Gorkhalis set up a base on Naikap to mount their assault on Kirtipur'; the first battle of Kirtipur is lost (Kalu Pande dies) and a peace treaty with Kathmandu follows in 1758, but the Gorkhali hold on the valley rim (Shivapuri 1759, the 1763 towns) continues to 1768.

region.text: Shivapuri, the hills on the north rim of the Nepal Valley, captured 1759

ledger.note: 1759: Shivapuri captured. Unification table, 1759 (1816 BS): 'Captures Shivapuri'. The page gives no whose-land or boundary; the hills north of the valley are my reading.

region.text: Makwanpur (the Sen kingdom, seat at Makwanpurgadhi near Hetauda) and Sindhuli, annexed 1762

ledger.note: August 1762: Makwanpur and Sindhuli annexed. The Gorkhalis 'launched an attack on 17 August 1762' on Makwanpur, 'ruled by the Sen dynasty'; table, 1762 (1819 BS): 'Makwanpur annexed, Sindhuli annexed'. The Prithvi Narayan Shah page's text says 'In 1763, the Gorkhas conquered' it and its table 'August 1762'.

region.text: Banepa, Dhulikhel, Sanga and Nala on the east rim of the valley, and Pharping on the south rim

ledger.note: 1763: the towns on the valley's east and south rim fall. Table, 1763 (1820 BS): 'Pharping, Bisankhu, Dhulikhel, Banepa, Sanga, Ranikot, Nala, Parevakot and Kavilaspur annexed.' The page does not say which kingdom held them; the two circles are my reading of the town names.

region.text: Kirtipur, the hill town south-west of Kathmandu, with Salimpa

ledger.note: March 1766: Kirtipur falls after three assaults. Table, 1766 (1823 BS): 'Kritipur captured, Salimpa annexed'; the Prithvi Narayan Shah page: Kirtipur 'conquered ... on his third attempt', table 'March 1766' (its text gives 1765 for the attack).

25 September 1768: Prithvi Narayan Shah takes Kathmandu. 'Prithvi Narayan Shah entered Kathmandu unopposed on 25 September 1768 during the Indra Jatra revelry'; Lalitpur falls in October 1768 and Bhaktapur in 1769, in the nepal dossier.

ledger.note: 25 September 1768: the fight for the valley's first city ends in the Gorkhali entry into Kathmandu; Lalitpur (October 1768) and Bhaktapur (1769) are the nepal dossier's.
1768: the capital passes from Gorkha to Kathmandu ('declared Kathmandu the capital of his unified kingdom'); the Unification table dates 'Kathmandu is declared as the capital' to 1769.

wars.name: Kinloch expedition (Battle of Sindhuli Gadhi)
wars.outcome: The expedition sent to help the king of Kathmandu 'completely miscarried': 'once the troops reached Sindhuli, the promised help collapsed' (September 1767, Battle of Sindhuli Gadhi). No border moved.
wars.note: The Gorkha Kingdom page: 'In 1767, the Company sent an expedition led by Captain George Kinloch, which failed before reaching Kathmandu.'

notes:
Cliopatria row 'Gorkha Kingdom' 1588-1787 (10 shapes, 148,000 km2 from the first year) is the modern outline of Nepal drawn back to 1588; every shape is marked wrong. The dossier rebuilds the state from three pages: a hill core around Gorkha (1559), then the dated annexations (Nuwakot 1744, Dolakha 1754, Shivapuri 1759, Makwanpur and Sindhuli 1762, the valley-rim towns 1763, Kirtipur 1766, Kathmandu 25 September 1768). It ends on 25 September 1768 with the Kingdom of Nepal, as the nepal dossier (sa-05-f) asks; the shapes of 1769-1787 are duplicates of that dossier (the 1775 and 1783 shapes are the western and northern half of the same country) and are marked wrong.
Page silent or in conflict: (1) no page dates growth before 1744; the 1559 core is a radius reading, the Dhading part rests on one phrase of the Prithvi Narayan Shah page. (2) Nuwakot: the table says 'returned to Kathmandu in 1745', the prose and the kathmandu dossier keep it; I follow the prose. (3) Kirtipur: 1765 (text) or March 1766 (table). (4) Unification table rows left out for lack of a location on the pages: 1761 'Chaule and Kahule is captured', 1765 'Balaju, Lutikot annexed', and 1768 'British India takes possession of Bara, Parsa and Hilwal / Gorkha repossess the territory. Annexes Bettia' (the Terai east of the Gandak; the month is not given); a gap-filler should look for them. (5) No reign years on the Gorkha page, so no ruler strip. (6) Accession year 1742 (table) or 3 April 1743 (text). Pages opened: 3 of up to 5.
Counterparts: kathmandu (Nuwakot loss 1744; the valley contest 1757-1768). Not in the gazetteer (places given as coordinates here): Gorkha, Nuwakot (the kathmandu dossier uses the name), Dolakha, Sindhupalchowk, Sindhuli, Kirtipur and Shivapuri; Hetauda and Kathmandu are present. States needing dossiers: Lalitpur (Patan) and Bhaktapur (kingdoms of the Nepal Valley, to 1768/1769; the kathmandu notes already ask), Makwanpur (Sen kingdom, to 1762), the Dolakha principality.
